metadata.name: IronManArena physically based lighting presets (contrib/vison)
metadata.engine_notes: Property names follow UE 5.x FPostProcessSettings / component UPROPERTY names (C++ spelling). A few may have been renamed in 5.8; apply_lighting_preset.py tries known aliases and skips/logs anything missing.

units.DirectionalLight.Intensity: lux (illuminance). With bAtmosphereSunLight, the sun value is top-of-atmosphere (120000 lux); the atmosphere applies transmittance. See _ground_illuminance_lux_approx for the value at the ground.
units.SkyLight.Intensity: scalar multiplier on the captured sky (1.0 = physically correct)
units.exposure: EV100 (ISO 100 reference). AutoExposureMinBrightness/MaxBrightness are EV100 because the project sets r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange=True
units.distances: centimetres (Unreal units): StartDistance, VolumetricFogDistance, Lumen distances, ManualFocusDistance, FogHeightOffset
units.cloud altitudes: kilometres (VolumetricCloud LayerBottomAltitude, LayerHeight; SkyAtmosphere exponential distributions)
units.CameraShutterSpeed: denominator in 1/s, the UE convention (48 means 1/48 s)
units.fog density: UE ExponentialHeightFog units (density at height 0, with falloff per km-scaled height)

conventions.colors: Linear RGB 0-1 as {R,G,B,A} (FLinearColor). Exception: VolumetricFogAlbedo and SkyAtmosphere GroundAlbedo are FColor (sRGB 8-bit) in UE, so they are stored linear here and converted on apply.
conventions.vector4_grading: Color grading values are FVector4 {X,Y,Z,W} = {R,G,B, luminance multiplier}. ColorGain etc. are RGBA in that sense.
conventions.rotation: {Pitch,Yaw,Roll} in degrees for the light actor. Pitch is negative when the light points down, so sun elevation = -Pitch. Positive Pitch puts the sun below the horizon. This matches FRotator(SunPitch, SunYaw, 0) in AArenaEnvironment::ApplyPreset.
conventions.keys: Keys are the UE C++ property names. Keys starting with '_' are informational (documentation, checks) and must not be applied. 'Rotation', 'Visible', 'SecondFogData', 'Cubemap', 'PostProcessOverrides', 'FilmbackPreset' are handled specially by the applier.
conventions.enums: Enum values use the C++ enumerator names (AEM_Histogram, BM_SOG, SLS_CapturedScene, Lumen, Tracking, Default/HitLighting). In Python they become UPPER_SNAKE (AEM_HISTOGRAM, LUMEN, HIT_LIGHTING).
conventions.lights: Two directional lights, as in the project's AArenaEnvironment: 'DirectionalLight' = Sun (AtmosphereSunLightIndex 0), 'MoonLight' = Moon (AtmosphereSunLightIndex 1). Night presets turn the sun off and the moon on. Light colour stays white; colour comes from Temperature plus atmosphere.
conventions.exposure_model: Gameplay: PostProcessVolume uses AEM_Histogram clamped to scene EV100 -1..+1.5 stops. Cutscenes: CineCamera.PostProcessOverrides uses AEM_Manual with AutoExposureApplyPhysicalCameraExposure, so EV100 = log2(N^2/t) - log2(ISO/100) where N = CurrentAperture, t = 1/CameraShutterSpeed, and ISO = CameraISO (ND folded in). Each preset's _exposure_check shows camera EV = scene EV within 0.15 stops.
conventions.scene_ev_from_lux: EV100 = log2(E / 2.5) for incident illuminance E in lux (meter calibration C = 250). Reference: 120000 lux = 15.6, 15000 lux = 12.6, 600 lux = 7.9, 40 lux = 4.0.
conventions.shutter: Shutter speed t = (shutter angle / 360) / fps. MotionBlurAmount = shutter angle / 360 (0.5 = 180 deg).
conventions.nd_filters: UE's physical camera has no ND. A real ND of n stops is represented as CameraISO = native ISO / 2^n (each 0.3 OD = 1 stop).

how_to_apply.python: In the editor (Python plugin enabled), open the level and run: py "<path>/contrib/vison/apply_lighting_preset.py" --preset city   (add --dry-run to preview, --list to list presets, --cine-camera <label> to target one CineCameraActor, --lux-scale 1e-4 to match the project's scaled-lux convention).
how_to_apply.cpp_project: To feed the game's runtime path instead, map fields to FEnvironmentPreset: SunPitch/SunYaw = DirectionalLight.Rotation; SunLux = DirectionalLight.Intensity * lux_scale; SunKelvin = DirectionalLight.Temperature; MoonLux = MoonLight.Intensity * lux_scale (0 if not Visible); SkyLightIntensity = SkyLight.Intensity; CloudBottomKm/CloudHeightKm = VolumetricCloud.LayerBottomAltitude/LayerHeight; FogDensity/FogHeightFalloff/FogColor = ExponentialHeightFog.FogDensity/FogHeightFalloff/FogInscatteringColor; VolumetricFogExtinction/VolumetricFogAlbedo; ExposureBias = AutoExposureBias; BloomIntensity; LensFlareIntensity; WhiteBalanceKelvin = WhiteTemp; Saturation/Contrast = ColorSaturation.W/ColorContrast.W; Gain = ColorGain.XYZ; Vignette = VignetteIntensity; FilmGrain = FilmGrainIntensity; ChromaticAberration = SceneFringeIntensity. Also set AutoExposureMinBrightness/MaxBrightness, which ApplyPreset does not set today.
how_to_apply.blueprint: Parse with the JsonBlueprintUtilities plugin (or C++ FJsonObjectConverter), then for each block call the setters (SetIntensity, SetTemperature, SetFogDensity, ...) and fill the PostProcessVolume Settings struct with the matching bOverride_ flags.

metadata.lux_scale_note: The game's C++ presets currently use scaled sun values (SunLux 4-10) with histogram auto exposure, and its emissive and local-light levels are tuned for that. These presets are physical (sun 120000 lux TOA). Either re-balance local lights and emissives to real-world levels (recommended for 'super realistic'), or apply with --lux-scale 1e-4. That multiplies the sun and moon by 1e-4 and shifts every EV100 value by log2(1e-4) = -13.29 stops, so the relative look is unchanged.

chapter_mapping._arena_note: Free-play 'arena' has no story look. Reuse 'city' or keep the project defaults.

time_of_day.phase: civil twilight (sun 4 deg below the horizon)

prologue.look: Tungsten work-lamp pools in a dark lake-house garage. Blue-hour windows, dust in the beams, the arc reactor as the coolest light in the room.

DirectionalLight._note: Sun below the horizon: no direct light (planet shadow via atmosphere transmittance), but it drives the blue-hour sky glow seen through the windows.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).
SkyAtmosphere._note: A slightly higher Mie value for the lake haze.

SkyLight._note: Real-time capture gives the dim blue sky that shows through the windows. Lumen does the interior bounce.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Second layer: mist on the lake outside, sitting below floor level. Volumetric: dust in the work-lamp cones.

_material_parameters.note: Mostly unseen and only matters through the windows. Keep the cloud material cheap (ViewSampleCountScale 0.5 is fine here).

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._note: Close and handheld-adjacent. Shoot at T2 so the work lamps fall into soft 9-blade bokeh.

rendering_notes.lumen: Interior: Final Gather 2 for gameplay and 4 for cinematics. SkylightLeaking 0.02 only stops the corners going pure black; raise it if the windows are small.
rendering_notes.vsm: The key light comes from local spots, so give the work lamps SourceRadius 2-5 cm for soft VSM penumbrae. r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayCountLocal 8 for cinematics.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Optional. HWRT Lumen (the project's menu toggle) improves the reflections in polished suit parts.

film_references: Iron Man (2008), the cave and the Malibu garage builds (DP Matthew Libatique)
Blade Runner 2049, interiors with dust shafts (Roger Deakins)
The Social Network, warm practicals (Jeff Cronenweth)

workshop.look: Clean daylight through skylights and clerestories meets warm tungsten practicals. Glossy floor, crisp reflections, a hopeful mood.

exposure_reference.key: interior lit by daylight and practicals

DirectionalLight._note: Outdoor ground value. Inside, the sun patches through the skylights land at about 60k-80k lux and clip by design (local exposure handles them).

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).

SkyLight._fallback: If the HDRI asset is missing, use SLS_CapturedScene + bRealTimeCapture true (the project's ApplyPreset does the same).
SkyLight._note: This matches the project, whose workshop sets bHdriSkyLight = true. Intensity 1.0 assumes the HDRI is calibrated so the sky is about 8k-15k cd/m2. Otherwise switch to real-time capture.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Fog is nearly zero inside. The volumetric fog makes the skylight shafts: a high forward-scattering G (0.75) means the beams only glow when you look toward the sun.

_material_parameters.note: Visible only through the skylights. Cloud shadows passing over the skylights give a nice slow light modulation.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._note: Large-format glass with a shallow-but-readable depth of field at T2.8 on the build table.

rendering_notes.lumen: Glossy floor and display cases: ReflectionQuality 2 plus front-layer translucency reflections for the glass suit cases (costly, so drop it in gameplay if needed).
rendering_notes.vsm: The sun through the skylights is the key light. Keep LightSourceAngle physical (0.53 deg) so the window-frame shadows stay crisp.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: HWRT plus LumenRayLightingMode HitLighting in cinematics gives accurate car-paint and suit reflections.

film_references: Iron Man (2008), Malibu workshop (Matthew Libatique)
Iron Man 3, Tony's workshop (John Toll)
Ex Machina, clean controlled interiors (Rob Hardy)

time_of_day.weather: clear with high altocumulus, urban haze

rooftops.look: Low amber sun skimming the skyline, long raking shadows, glowing haze between the towers. Exhilarating and wide.

DirectionalLight._note: The atmosphere does the reddening and dimming. Do NOT lower Temperature as well, or the colour gets applied twice. Yaw 255 matches the project's rooftops_dusk.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).
SkyAtmosphere._note: Urban aerosol haze: a stronger Mie value and a longer aerial perspective so the skyline layers recede into gold.

SkyLight._note: Warm bounce off the concrete rooftops.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: The falloff matches the project (0.12). Volumetric G 0.7 for shafts between the towers.

_material_parameters.note: Altitude and height match the project's rooftops_dusk (3 km / 4 km). Raise the MultiScattering Contribution in the material so the undersides glow.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 2.1 (7 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^7 = 6.25
CineCamera._note: 2x anamorphic, desqueezed to 2.39:1: oval bokeh, horizontal flares from the sun and repulsors, gentle edge fringing. Focal lengths are as marked on the lens; the horizontal field of view equals half that focal length on spherical glass.

rendering_notes.lumen: At golden hour the bounce dominates the shadow side, so the default gameplay quality is enough. Use the cinematic overrides for hero shots.
rendering_notes.vsm: Grazing sun means very long shadows. Raise r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages (8192) if the far rooftops lose shadow detail.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Optional. Glass towers benefit from HWRT reflections.

film_references: Top Gun: Maverick, golden-hour aerials (Claudio Miranda)
Man of Steel, first flight (Amir Mokri)
Spider-Man: Far From Home, rooftops (Matthew J. Lloyd)

city.display_name: City by Day: Static in the Wires
city.look: Hard, clean summer daylight. Deep blue sky, crisp shadows, glass towers flaring. Grounded and documentary-real, like IMAX daylight.

DirectionalLight._note: Yaw 30 matches the project's city_day. Ground illuminance is about 105k lux direct plus 15k from the sky.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).

SkyLight._note: Lower hemisphere: sun-lit asphalt and concrete (albedo about 0.12-0.2).

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Only a little haze, mostly from the SkyAtmosphere. Keep the fog thin so distant towers keep contrast.

_material_parameters.note: Small, bright, hard-edged clouds. Their shadows sweeping over the city are a strong realism cue.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 2.4 (8 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^8 = 3.125
CineCamera._note: IMAX 70mm frame: a 80 mm lens frames like about 32 mm on Super 35. At f/5.6 the depth of field is still shallow because of the huge sensor. 8 stops of ND are folded into the ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: Large outdoor area: SceneViewDistance and MaxTraceDistance at 300 m. Distant towers rely on the Lumen far field (r.LumenScene.FarField 1, needs HWRT) or the skylight.
rendering_notes.vsm: VSM with a physical sun angle gives crisp contact shadows. Raise MaxPhysicalPages to 8192 or more for the skyline. Nanite facades are required for VSM caching to stay cheap.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Recommended for the glass curtain walls (HWRT reflections plus far field).

film_references: Avengers: Endgame, daylight NYC (Trent Opaloch, IMAX digital)
The Dark Knight, IMAX daylight Chicago (Wally Pfister)
Captain America: The Winter Soldier, DC streets (Trent Opaloch)

ruins.look: Smoke-filtered tan sunlight, dusty air, bleached and desaturated. A gritty war-documentary feel with a staccato shutter.

DirectionalLight._note: Pitch and yaw match the project's ruins. LightSourceAngle is widened from the physical 0.53 deg to 1.2 to mimic forward scattering in smoke, which softens the VSM penumbrae. The smoke dimming comes from the SkyAtmosphere Mie absorption and the fog.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).
SkyAtmosphere._note: Smoke and dust aerosol: strong Mie scattering plus absorption, concentrated low (2 km scale height).

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Density and falloff match the project's ruins. The second layer is ground-hugging dust. The albedo is warm ash.

_material_parameters.note: Altitude and height match the project (1 km / 3 km). Darken the albedo for a smoke-stained look.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 1.5 (5 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^5 = 25
CineCamera._note: A 90-degree shutter (1/96 s) gives staccato debris and muzzle flashes. MotionBlurAmount 0.25 matches it. 5 stops of ND are folded into the ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: Gameplay defaults. The dust albedo and Lumen bounce give the warm fill.
rendering_notes.vsm: The softer sun angle hides VSM aliasing on rubble. Nanite rubble keeps VSM caching efficient.

film_references: Saving Private Ryan, narrow shutter and bleach bypass (Janusz Kaminski)
Black Hawk Down (Slawomir Idziak)
Children of Men, Bexhill battle (Emmanuel Lubezki)

time_of_day.phase: late afternoon (sun 14 deg up), heavily smoke-filtered

titan_battlefield.look: Apocalyptic orange sun through a smoke pall, fire-lit haze, silhouetted Titan, teal shadows against ember highlights. Epic scale.

DirectionalLight._note: Pitch and yaw match the project's battlefield. The heavy aerosol in the SkyAtmosphere dims and reddens the sun to about 2800 K perceived. Volumetric scattering is at 2 for god rays through the smoke.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).
SkyAtmosphere._note: A thick smoke pall: strong Mie scattering and absorption.

SkyLight._note: Scorched ground bounce, warmed by the fires.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Density, falloff and colour family match the project's battlefield. Fire-lit smoke inscattering. Put Local Fog Volumes around the big fires and let their point lights scatter.

_material_parameters.note: Dark, low, heavy. Optionally add an emissive bottom term of about 0.01 orange for fire light on the underside.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 0.9 (3 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^3 = 100
CineCamera._note: IMAX for scale against the Titan, with a 90-degree shutter for punchy action. 3 stops of ND are folded into the ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: Explosions and fires change fast: update speeds are at 3. The emissive fire and lava need real point lights as well (Lumen alone lags and is noisy).
rendering_notes.vsm: Many shadowed fire lights: use MegaLights (5.5+) or cap the shadow casters. The sun's 2 deg angle gives soft, smoky shadows.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Optional. The Titan's obsidian surface gains from HWRT reflections in cinematics.

film_references: Avengers: Endgame, final battle (Trent Opaloch)
Mad Max: Fury Road (John Seale)
Dunkirk, IMAX (Hoyte van Hoytema)

DirectionalLight._note: Yaw 90 (east) matches the project's finale_dawn. The pitch is lowered from -6 to -3 for a true sunrise. The atmosphere gives about 3300 K at the ground.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note: Residual smoke, much lighter than titan_battlefield.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Density 0.02 and extinction 1.0 match the project's finale_dawn. The second layer is mist pooled in the craters.

VolumetricCloud._cloud_type: altocumulus lit from below by the rising sun

_material_parameters.note: Pink/gold undersides: raise MultiScattering Contribution and Occlusion.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 1.2 (4 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^4 = 50
CineCamera._note: A wide, still IMAX frame for the ending. FFT bloom for an accurate sun-disc glare. 4 stops of ND are folded into the ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: Gameplay defaults. Use cinematic overrides for the ending.
rendering_notes.vsm: Grazing sun: the very long shadows need MaxPhysicalPages of 8192 or more.

film_references: The Revenant, natural dawn light (Emmanuel Lubezki)
Avengers: Endgame, lake-house epilogue (Trent Opaloch)
Dunkirk (Hoyte van Hoytema)

rendering_notes.lumen: The emissive screens and holograms ARE the lighting, so Lumen picks them up (they need to emit about 50-200 cd/m2 to light the room plausibly). Update speeds are at 2 for flickering screens.
rendering_notes.vsm: The moon casts the window-mullion shadows. Screens give no shadows, so add a couple of shadowed rect lights over the monitor banks.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: HitLighting gives accurate hologram reflections on the suit.

rooftops_storm.display_name: Rooftops in a Storm: Siege of the Skyline

time_of_day.weather: thunderstorm, heavy rain, low cloud base

rooftops_storm.look: Wet black concrete, rain streaks backlit by city glow, a low orange-grey cloud ceiling and lightning flashes. Ominous and kinetic.

exposure_reference.key: rooftop lit by city spill and practicals

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.
MoonLight._note: The moon is physically present, but cloud shadows (coverage 0.95) reduce it to almost nothing. Lightning: briefly spawn or flash a second directional or rect light at about 50-500 lux for 50-150 ms, colour temperature about 7500 K.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).

SkyLight._note: The night sky is nearly black. City skyglow comes from the fog inscattering colour and the emissive windows.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Density and falloff match the project's rooftops_storm. The inscattering is warm-grey skyglow from sodium and LED light bouncing off the cloud base. The high extinction stands in for rain.

_material_parameters.note: Base 0.9 km, matching the project. To get the city-lit underside, add a small emissive or ambient term (for example 0.02 warm) in the cloud material, or rely on the fog colour.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._note: Same anamorphic package as First Flight, so the two rooftop chapters cut together. Wide open, with rain streaks against lit windows.

rendering_notes.lumen: Lightning needs fast GI response: update speeds are at 4. Wet roughness of about 0.1 makes Lumen reflections carry the scene.
rendering_notes.vsm: Few shadowed lights. Give the lightning light VSM shadows, but keep it short so the page cache isn't thrashed.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Strongly recommended: HWRT reflections on wet rooftops (screen traces break at the frame edges).

film_references: The Batman, wet night city (Greig Fraser)
Blade Runner 2049, LA rain (Roger Deakins)
Pacific Rim, rain-soaked night battles (Guillermo Navarro)

city_night._kind: chapter variant (the project already defines this look)
city_night.display_name: City at Night: Eyes in the Dark
city_night.look: Sodium-orange and LED-white pools on wet asphalt, a teal-blue moonlit ambience, haloed streetlamps. Paranoid and noir.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).

SkyLight._note: The moonlit sky is near-black. The fill comes from the fog skyglow plus Lumen bounce off lit facades.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Matches the project's city_night (0.025 / 0.15) at a slightly lower density. Volumetric G 0.6 gives halos and cones under the streetlamps.

_material_parameters.note: Moonlit edges. A small warm ambient term in the material simulates city light on the cloud bases.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._note: Shot like digital-cinema night work: wide open at T2 and ISO 1250, so the streetlights become bokeh. The grain matches the high ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: Many emissive windows: rely on Lumen for their contribution but keep the key lights as real lights. Wet roads need ReflectionQuality 2.
rendering_notes.vsm: Many shadowed streetlights. Consider MegaLights (r.MegaLights.EnableForProject, 5.5+) or limit shadow casters to lights near the player.
rendering_notes.ray_tracing: Recommended: HWRT reflections on wet asphalt and glass.

film_references: Collateral, digital night LA (Dion Beebe, Paul Cameron)
The Batman (Greig Fraser)
Nightcrawler (Robert Elswit)

city_overcast._kind: chapter variant (the project already defines this look)
city_overcast.look: Soft, shadowless grey light, damp streets, muted colour. Reflective and somber, with a cool neutral palette.

DirectionalLight._note: Pitch and yaw match the project's city_overcast. The sun is physical above the clouds; the 0.95 cloud coverage and cloud shadows make the ground diffuse. If your cloud material doesn't block enough, lower Intensity to about 10000 and leave the SkyLight at 1.

MoonLight._note_color: Moonlight is reflected sunlight, slightly warmer than daylight (~4100 K). It reads blue because the camera WhiteTemp is set below it, not because the light is tinted. Light color stays white.

SkyAtmosphere._note_name: AerialPespectiveViewDistanceScale is spelled this way in UE source (sic).

SkyLight._note: Under overcast the SkyLight carries most of the illumination. Real-time capture is essential so it picks up the cloud deck.

ExponentialHeightFog._note_inscattering: UE 5.1+ stores this as FogInscatteringLuminance (same linear colour); the setter is still SetFogInscatteringColor. Keep it low when SkyAtmosphere affects height fog (project enables r.SupportSkyAtmosphereAffectsHeightFog).
ExponentialHeightFog._note_albedo: VolumetricFogAlbedo is an FColor (8-bit sRGB) in UE: convert this linear value with ToFColor(true), as ArenaEnvironment.cpp does.
ExponentialHeightFog._note: Density and falloff match the project's city_overcast. The second layer is low street-level mist.

_material_parameters.note: A low, flat, uniform deck. Reduce the detail noise and erosion in the material.

PostProcessVolume._note_exposure: Min/Max are EV100 because the project enables r.DefaultFeature.AutoExposure.ExtendDefaultLuminanceRange. Min EV100 is the clamp that stops dark scenes being brightened to grey.

CineCamera._nd_filter: ND 1.8 (6 stops); UE has no ND, so it is folded into CameraISO = 800 / 2^6 = 12.5
CineCamera._note: Contemplative longer lenses (58-125 mm). 6 stops of ND are folded into the ISO.

rendering_notes.lumen: The diffuse sky dominates. Lumen skylight occlusion (SkylightLeaking 0) gives grounded contact darkening.
rendering_notes.vsm: The sun is heavily attenuated, so its shadows are faint. Shadow quality matters less here than SSAO and Lumen AO.

film_references: Sicario, flat overcast (Roger Deakins)
Children of Men (Emmanuel Lubezki)
Captain America: Civil War, Berlin/Leipzig (Trent Opaloch)
